bib.title: Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed for origins only; figure bar values are chart-label numbers without axis context.

question: Do o1-like reasoning models think deeply enough, or do they abandon promising lines of reasoning too early, and can decoding fix it?
hypothesis: Frequent thought switching in incorrect responses reflects underthinking (abandoning correct thoughts) rather than lack of understanding; penalising switch tokens should raise accuracy without fine-tuning.
contributions: Formally define and characterize the underthinking issue in o1-like LLMs
Introduce a metric of token efficiency in incorrect responses (underthinking score)
Propose TIP, a decoding thought switching penalty that improves accuracy without fine-tuning

method.summary: Segment long CoT of o1-like models into thoughts at switch phrases such as 'alternatively' using Llama-3.3-70B, judge each thought's correctness with two R1-distilled models, and define an underthinking score from the tokens after the first correct thought. TIP subtracts a constant alpha from logits of switch tokens for beta positions after each thought starts.
method.task: hard math and science QA with long chain-of-thought reasoning models; decoding-time intervention

datasets.name: AIME2022-23
datasets.split: development set for grid search over alpha and beta

other.note: web interface, 50 messages/day, so only MATH500 and AIME
no training; TIP is decode-time only

inference.decoding: TIP: z_hat = z - alpha for switch tokens while t < Psi + beta
inference.samples: 32 samples per problem; Pass@1 computed from the 32
inference.prompting: Persistence prompt (context, solving rules, format rules blocks) for the DeepSeek-R1 + PROMPT row; other runs unstated

metrics.name: Accuracy (Pass@k)
metrics.definition: Pass@1 from 32 samples per instance; Pass@4/8/16 also reported

metrics.name: Underthinking score xi_UT
metrics.definition: mean over incorrect responses of 1 - T_hat/T, T_hat = tokens up to and including the first correct thought (T_hat=T if none)

metrics.name: Weighted UT score
metrics.definition: mean over 32 samples per instance of xi_UT, 0 for correct samples

metrics.name: Switching tokens
metrics.definition: average count of thought-switch tokens per response, plus average interval between them

eval.protocol: 32 samples per problem; thought correctness by two LLM judges (correct if either gives score 2); judge validated on 90 final thoughts from QwQ (35 correct, 55 incorrect); no significance test reported; weighted UT given as mean±std over samples

evidence.quote: we generated 32 responses with a temperature of 0.7 and a top p value of 0.95
We selected α = 3 and β = 600 for our subsequent experiments.

results.claim: Incorrect responses from o1-like models use far more tokens and switch thoughts far more often than correct ones.
results.metric: extra tokens in incorrect vs correct
results.setup: AIME2024; QwQ-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1-Preview, DeepSeek-R1-671B (averaged); conventional LLMs Qwen-Math-72B and Llama3.3-70B show no significant length gap
results.quote: On average, o1-like LLMs consume 225% more tokens in incorrect responses than in correct ones due to 418% more frequent thought-switching behaviors.

results.claim: A prompt asking for thought persistence barely changes DeepSeek-R1 accuracy or switching.
results.setup: DeepSeek-R1, AIME2024, 32 samples, T=0.7, top-p 0.95; one prompt, one model; switch tokens 13.8 -> 12.0, interval 580.1 -> 520.1; TIP gives 74.8 and 5.7
results.quote: Although prompt engineering (DeepSeek-R1 + PROMPT) provides certain guidance, Table 3 shows only modest changes in switching tokens and overall accuracy compared with TIP.

results.claim: TIP raises QwQ-32B-Preview accuracy on AIME2024.
results.setup: QwQ-32B-Preview, AIME2024, alpha=3, beta=600 tuned on AIME2022-23 with QwQ, 32 samples
results.quote: Clearly, our approach consistently improves accuracy over the vanilla QwQ-32B-Preview in all cases by mitigating the underthinking issues.

results.claim: TIP gives a small gain on DeepSeek-R1 AIME2024 and halves switch tokens.
results.setup: DeepSeek-R1, AIME2024, same alpha/beta; switch tokens 13.8 to 5.7, interval 580.1 to 941.6 tokens; Pass@16 unchanged at 89.8
results.quote: the number of thought-switching tokens for DeepSeek- R1 dramatically decreases from 13.8 to 5.7 when using the TIP method, and the average interval increases from 580.1 to 941.6 tokens

results.claim: Gains from TIP on MATH500-Hard and GPQA Diamond are small (about 0.6 and 1.5 points Pass@1).
results.quote: Clearly, our approach consistently improves accuracy over the vanilla QwQ-32B-Preview in all cases by mitigating the underthinking issues.

results.claim: Over 70% of incorrect responses contain at least one correct thought that was not finished.
results.metric: share of incorrect responses with a correct thought
results.setup: three models on the three hard test sets; correctness judged by two R1-distilled models
results.quote: We observe that over 70% of incorrect responses contain at least one correct thought. Furthermore, in more than 50% of these responses, over 10% of the thoughts are correct.

results.claim: The LLM thought-correctness judge agrees with final-answer labels about 82% of the time.
results.metric: judge accuracy on correct / incorrect thoughts
results.setup: 90 final thoughts from QwQ-32B-Preview on AIME 2022-24; 35 correct and 55 incorrect, length-matched (278.1 vs 278.3 tokens); incorrect-class accuracy 81.8%
results.quote: Our assessment approach achieves accuracies of 82.9% for correct examples and 81.8% for incorrect examples

results.claim: Higher accuracy of the larger model does not imply less underthinking: R1-671B has higher UT than QwQ on MATH500-Hard and GPQA but lower on AIME24.
results.quote: The larger model's superior capabilities do not uniformly translate to less underthinking across all tasks.

results.claim: TIP combined with Self-Consistency lifts QwQ AIME2024 accuracy at 4 samples.
results.setup: QwQ-32B-Preview, AIME2024, 4 samples, 10,000 trials over the 32 samples
results.quote: the TIP method enhances the Pass@4 accuracy of QwQ-32B-Preview from 43.7% to 51.4% on the AIME2024 dataset

results.claim: Laconic Decoding (shortest of N) beats Self-Consistency for R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, and TIP adds to it.
results.quote: the Pass@4 accuracy of R1-Distill-Qwen-32B increases from 74.4% to 78.0%, while the Underthinking Score decreases from 8.7 to 7.3
results.where: p.12 (text says Pass@4; Table 4 shows these at 8 samples)

results.claim: Longer penalty duration at low alpha helps; at high alpha it hurts.
results.quote: At a lower penalty strength (α = 3), increasing β from 300 to 600 results in accuracy gains from 35.2% to 39.8%

limits: Hyperparameters alpha and beta were tuned on AIME2022-23 with QwQ-32B-Preview only, then reused for R1 and R1-Distill-Qwen.
Persistence prompt tested on one model (DeepSeek-R1) and one prompt on one dataset; the authors say better prompt engineering may do more and that prompt plus decoding could combine.
Needs logit access to penalise switch tokens; the switch token set is a hand-gathered list from QwQ outputs (e.g. 'alternatively'), so it may not transfer to other model families.
Thought correctness and segmentation depend on LLM judges validated at about 82% on 90 final thoughts only; Table 4 text says Pass@4 where table rows show other sample counts.
Gains on MATH500-Hard and GPQA are under 2 points Pass@1; no significance tests reported. Models studied are 2025-era open o1-like models (QwQ-Preview, R1), which have since been superseded.
Authors call this an initial exploration; claims are about math and science QA only. The paper says Pass@k UT score is infeasible to compute so means are reported.

code.snippet:
<solving rules>
- Try to complete every idea you think of and don't give up halfway
- Don't skip steps
- Display solution process clearly
- Ask for clarification on ambiguity
</solving rules>
z_hat[t,v] = z[t,v] - alpha if v in V_hat and t < Psi + beta else z[t,v]
